'''Margaret Mary Sheil''' is an Australian academic and the [[Vice-chancellor|Vice Chancellor]] of [[Queensland University of Technology]].<ref name="auto2">{{cite web|title=QUT announces New Vice Chancellor|url=https://www.qut.edu.au/news?news-id=122716|access-date=15 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180815133037/https://www.qut.edu.au/news?news-id=122716|archive-date=15 August 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Early years==
Margaret Sheil was born in [[Goulburn]], New South Wales<ref>{{cite web |title=Sheil, Margaret Mary (1961 - ) |url=https://www.eoas.info/biogs/P006061b.htm |website=Encyclopedia of Australian Science}}</ref> in August 1961. As a teenager, she regularly visited the Department of Chemistry at the [[University of New South Wales]] (UNSW) where her mother, a nurse, was [[Secondment|seconded]] to work on a scientific study to monitor lead levels in the blood of children exposed to petroleum. Sheil earned a [[Bachelor of Science]] and a PhD in Physical Chemistry from UNSW.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web|url=https://theconversation.com/profiles/margaret-sheil-14167|title=Margaret Sheil|website=The Conversation|language=en|access-date=2017-08-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170818173424/https://theconversation.com/profiles/margaret-sheil-14167|archive-date=18 August 2017|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="auto4">{{Cite news|url=http://australiaindonesiacentre.org/people/professor-margaret-sheil/|title=Professor Margaret Sheil - Australia-Indonesia Centre|publisher=Australia-Indonesia Centre|access-date=2017-08-19|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170819062720/http://australiaindonesiacentre.org/people/professor-margaret-sheil/|archive-date=19 August 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> Sheil accepted her first post-doctoral position at the [[University of Utah]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://mcdonnellsymposium.wustl.edu/speaker/margaret-sheil/|title=Margaret Sheil - The Role of Research Universities in Addressing Global Challenges -|work=McDonnell|access-date=2017-08-19|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170818180419/https://mcdonnellsymposium.wustl.edu/speaker/margaret-sheil/|archive-date=18 August 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> followed by another at the [[Australian National University]].<ref name="auto3"/>

== University ==
Returning to Australia in 1990, Sheil accepted a lectureship in chemistry at the [[University of Wollongong]]. She was promoted to Professor of Chemistry in 2000, the first female chemistry professor in Australia,<ref name="auto5">{{Cite web|url=http://media.uow.edu.au/news/UOW106867.html|title=Women in chemistry inspire memorial lecture|website=media.uow.edu.au|language=en-au|others=jbradwel|access-date=2017-08-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170819062609/http://media.uow.edu.au/news/UOW106867.html|archive-date=19 August 2017|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Formula for Success|last=Carty|first=Lisa|date=5 May 2000|work=Illawarra Mercury}}</ref> before becoming dean of science in 2001.<ref name="auto6">{{Cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/person.asp?personId=39280266&privcapId=5510612&previousCapId=204604732&previousTitle=Coursera,%20Inc.|title=Margaret Sheil BSc (Hons), Ph.D., FRACI, FTSE, FANZSMS: Executive Profile & Biography|publisher=Bloomberg|access-date=2017-08-18}}</ref> The University of Wollongong Council appointed her to the role of Pro Vice-Chancellor (Research) in 2002, and then Deputy Vice-Chancellor (DVC Research) in 2005.<ref name="auto6"/> As DVC Research, Sheil led a major change at the University of Wollongong with the aim of boosting research outcomes and developing a high performance research culture. She has been acknowledged for boosting the national/international research reputation of the university, and supporting female academics, during her time at the University of Wollongong.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://media.uow.edu.au/news/UOW032748.html|title=Professor Sheil farewelled in style|website=media.uow.edu.au|language=en-au|others=bgoldie|access-date=2017-08-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170819062444/http://media.uow.edu.au/news/UOW032748.html|archive-date=19 August 2017|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="auto7">{{Cite web|url=http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/download?doi=10.1.1.521.8764&rep=rep1&type=pdf|title=A history of mass spectrometry in Australia|website=citeseerx.ist.psu.edu|access-date=2017-08-19}}{{dead link|date=February 2024|bot=medic}}</ref>

== Recognition and awards ==
Sheil received the ''Morrison Lecture'' for her contributions to [[mass spectrometry]] in Australia,<ref name="auto7"/> and was a finalist in the [[Australian Financial Review|AFR]] 100 women of Influence for 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.100womenofinfluence.com.au/alumni/2012-2/|title=2012 Event {{!}} 100 Women of Influence|website=100womenofinfluence.com.au|language=en-AU|access-date=2017-08-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170828132101/http://www.100womenofinfluence.com.au/alumni/2012-2/|archive-date=28 August 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> The Royal Australian Chemical Institute's ''Margaret Sheil Leadership award'' was established in recognition of her work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.raci.org.au/events-awards/young-chemists/margaret-sheil-leadership-award|title=Margaret Sheil Leadership Award - The Royal Australian Chemical Institute Incorporated|website=raci.org.au|access-date=2017-08-19}}</ref>

She is a Fellow of the [[Royal Australian Chemical Institute]] (RACI),<ref name="auto5" /><ref name="auto9">{{Cite web|last=Melbourne|first=The University of|date=2012-07-13|title=Provost: Chancellery (Academic & International)|url=http://provost.unimelb.edu.au/leadership/provost|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160813051943/http://provost.unimelb.edu.au/leadership/provost|archive-date=13 August 2016|access-date=2017-08-18|website=provost.unimelb.edu.au|language=en}}</ref> the [[Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering]] (ATSE),<ref name="auto9" /> and was made an inaugural fellow of the Australian and New Zealand Society for Mass Spectrometry (ANZSMS) in February 2014.<ref name="auto5" /><ref name="auto9" />

In 2017, she was appointed an Officer of the [[Order of Australia]], for services to science and education.<ref name="auto1" /><ref name="auto">{{Cite news|title=HIGH WIRED; Queens Birthday Honours|last=Kudich|first=Zsolt|date=12 June 2017|work=The Australian}}</ref> She was elected a Fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Science]] in May 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-05-25|title=Twenty-two Australians recognised among our nation's most distinguished scientists {{!}} Australian Academy of Science|url=https://www.science.org.au/news-and-events/news-and-media-releases/twenty-two-australians-recognised-among-nations-distinguished-scientists|access-date=2021-09-23|website=science.org.au|language=en}}</ref>

== Controversy ==

Shiel has faced criticism for her leadership as vice-chancellor at [[Queensland University of Technology]], which educates more than 52,000 students each year and employs 12,000 staff. She was the highest paid Queensland university VC in 2020 with a package worth at least $1.2m.{{citation needed|date=June 2025}}

In response to claims that a lavish personal bathroom had been constructed at the university, during cuts for staff and programs, Sheil stated, "one private bathroom plus an end-of-trip facility had been added during renovations to the heritage-listed Chancellery building, as were some marble finishes in public spaces as recommended by heritage architects".<ref>[https://www.couriermail.com.au/education-queensland/increasingly-toxic-culture-bullying-accusations-at-major-qld-university/news-story/d3a677ea195add95cd5a92223314171c 'Toxic culture': Bullying accusations at major Qld uni] ''The Courier Mail'' (subscription required)</ref>

Sheil gained attention for her support of Queensland University of Technology's decision to remove all references to the word "merit" from its hiring policy, claiming that such terminology never achieves its stated goals and preferring instead to move towards a more "inclusive suitability assessment".<ref>[https://www.abc.net.au/news/2023-11-17/qut-defends-removing-merit-from-hiring-policy/103114562 Queensland University of Technology defends removing 'merit' from hiring policy] ''Australian Broadcasting Corporation''</ref>
